body.id: Lebih dari seabad lalu, banyak anak perempuan di Hindia Belanda harus berhenti sekolah. Dua perempuan mengubah cerita itu: Kartini dari Jepara dan Dewi Sartika dari Bandung.
body.en: More than a century ago, many girls in the Dutch East Indies had to leave school. Two women changed that story: Kartini from Jepara and Dewi Sartika from Bandung.

body.id: Kisah di modul ini digambar sebagai siluet dan benda-benda dari karya mereka, tanpa wajah. Setiap kisah memakai sumber yang bisa diperiksa.
body.en: The stories in this module are drawn as silhouettes and the objects of their work, never faces. Every story uses sources you can check.

body.id: Integritas berarti berbuat benar walau tidak ada yang melihat, dan tetap setia pada prinsip.
body.en: Integrity means doing what is right even when no one is watching, and staying true to your principles.

body.id: Ki Hajar Dewantara menjaganya lewat tulisan dan sekolah. Mohammad Hatta menjaganya lewat kejujuran dalam hal-hal kecil.
body.en: Ki Hajar Dewantara kept it through his writing and his school. Mohammad Hatta kept it through honesty in small things.

body.id: Sejak lama, laut menghubungkan Nusantara dengan dunia. Pedagang, pelaut, dan pengelana datang membawa barang, kabar, dan ilmu.
body.en: For centuries the sea has linked the archipelago with the world. Traders, sailors and travellers came with goods, news and knowledge.

body.id: Ibn Battuta singgah di Samudra Pasai sekitar 1345. Armada Zheng He singgah di Jawa dan Sumatra pada 1405–1433.
body.en: Ibn Battuta stopped at Samudra Pasai around 1345. Zheng He's fleets called at Java and Sumatra between 1405 and 1433.

ST-A-KARTINI.source: Britannica: Kartini, Raden Ajeng; Encyclopedia.com: Kartini, Raden Ajeng; Kartini, Door Duisternis tot Licht (disunting J.H. Abendanon, 1911); Keppres No. 108 Tahun 1964

caption.id: Kartini lahir pada 21 April 1879 di Mayong, Jepara, dalam keluarga bangsawan Jawa. Ia bersekolah di sekolah Belanda dan gemar membaca.
caption.en: Kartini was born on 21 April 1879 in Mayong, Jepara, into a Javanese noble family. She went to a Dutch school and loved to read.

caption.id: Sekitar usia 12 tahun, ia harus berhenti sekolah dan tinggal di rumah, sesuai adat bagi gadis bangsawan saat itu. Kartini sangat ingin terus belajar.
caption.en: At about 12 she had to leave school and stay at home, as custom required of noble girls then. Kartini badly wanted to keep learning.

caption.id: Dari rumah, ia menulis surat kepada sahabat-sahabatnya di Belanda. Ia menulis tentang kehidupan perempuan Jawa dan harapannya agar anak perempuan boleh bersekolah.
caption.en: From home she wrote letters to friends in the Netherlands. She wrote about the lives of Javanese women and her hope that girls could go to school.

caption.id: Pada 1903, Kartini membuka kelas kecil untuk anak perempuan di rumah keluarganya di Jepara. Setelah menikah dengan Bupati Rembang akhir tahun itu, ia juga mengajar di Rembang.
caption.en: In 1903 Kartini opened a small class for girls in her family's home in Jepara. After marrying the Regent of Rembang late that year, she taught in Rembang too.

caption.id: Kartini wafat pada 1904, dalam usia 25 tahun. Pada 1911, surat-suratnya terbit sebagai buku, kelak dikenal dalam bahasa Indonesia sebagai «Habis Gelap Terbitlah Terang».
caption.en: Kartini died in 1904, aged just 25. In 1911 her letters came out as a book, later known in Indonesian as "Habis Gelap Terbitlah Terang" (After Darkness Comes Light).

caption.id: Hari lahirnya, 21 April, diperingati sebagai Hari Kartini. Kisahnya mengajak kita mendukung setiap anak, laki-laki maupun perempuan, untuk terus belajar.
caption.en: Her birthday, 21 April, is celebrated as Kartini Day. Her story asks us to help every child, girl or boy, keep learning.

title.en: Dewi Sartika and the School for Girls

ST-A-DEWI-SARTIKA.source: detikEdu: Sekolah Perempuan Pertama Indonesia Ada di Bandung (2023); GoodNewsFromIndonesia: Biografi Raden Dewi Sartika (2025); Keppres No. 252 Tahun 1966

caption.id: Dewi Sartika lahir pada 4 Desember 1884 di Bandung, dalam keluarga bangsawan Sunda. Orang tuanya menyekolahkannya di sekolah Belanda, hal yang jarang bagi anak perempuan saat itu.
caption.en: Dewi Sartika was born on 4 December 1884 in Bandung, into a Sundanese noble family. Her parents sent her to a Dutch school, which was rare for girls then.

caption.id: Sejak kecil ia suka bermain sekolah-sekolahan. Ia mengajari anak-anak para abdi membaca dan menulis, memakai papan, arang, dan pecahan genting.
caption.en: As a child she loved playing school. She taught the servants' children to read and write, using boards, charcoal and bits of roof tile.

caption.id: Saat itu, sangat sedikit anak perempuan yang bisa bersekolah. Dewi Sartika ingin mereka bisa membaca, berhitung, dan punya keterampilan.
caption.en: At the time very few girls could go to school. Dewi Sartika wanted them to read, count and learn practical skills.

caption.id: Pada 16 Januari 1904, dengan dukungan Bupati Bandung, ia membuka Sakola Istri di pendopo kabupaten. Kelas pertamanya berisi 20 murid perempuan.
caption.en: On 16 January 1904, with the support of the Regent of Bandung, she opened Sakola Istri (School for Girls) at the regency hall. Its first class had 20 girls.

caption.id: Murid-muridnya belajar membaca, menulis, dan berhitung, juga menjahit, memasak, dan membatik. Pada 1910 sekolah itu berganti nama menjadi Sakola Kautamaan Istri.
caption.en: Pupils learned reading, writing and arithmetic, and also sewing, cooking and batik. In 1910 the school was renamed Sakola Kautamaan Istri (School of Women's Virtue).

caption.id: Dewi Sartika wafat pada 1947 dan diangkat menjadi Pahlawan Nasional pada 1966. Kisahnya mengingatkan kita bahwa ilmu yang dibagikan bisa mengubah hidup banyak orang.
caption.en: Dewi Sartika died in 1947 and was named a National Hero in 1966. Her story reminds us that shared knowledge can change many lives.

title.id: Ki Hajar Dewantara dan Taman Siswa
title.en: Ki Hajar Dewantara and Taman Siswa

ST-A-KI-HAJAR.source: Kompas.id: Lost Traces of Ki Hadjar Dewantara and Tamansiswa (2022); Republika: Taman Siswa, legasi Ki Hajar Dewantara (2026); Wikipedia: Ki Hajar Dewantara; Keppres No. 305 Tahun 1959

caption.id: Ki Hajar Dewantara lahir di Yogyakarta pada 2 Mei 1889 dengan nama Raden Mas Soewardi Soerjaningrat. Ia menjadi wartawan yang menulis dengan berani.
caption.en: Ki Hajar Dewantara was born in Yogyakarta on 2 May 1889 as Raden Mas Soewardi Soerjaningrat. He became a journalist who wrote boldly.

caption.id: Pada 1913, ia menulis artikel «Seandainya Aku Seorang Belanda». Ia mengkritik rencana pemerintah kolonial memungut sumbangan dari warga, termasuk bumiputra, untuk merayakan 100 tahun kemerdekaan Belanda.
caption.en: In 1913 he wrote the article "If I Were a Dutchman". It criticised the colonial government's plan to collect money from residents, including Indonesians, to celebrate 100 years of Dutch independence.

caption.id: Karena tulisan itu, ia dibuang ke Belanda. Di sana ia memakai waktunya untuk belajar ilmu pendidikan hingga meraih ijazah guru.
caption.en: Because of that article he was exiled to the Netherlands. There he used his time to study education and earned a teaching certificate.

caption.id: Ia pulang pada 1919, lalu pada 3 Juli 1922 mendirikan Taman Siswa di Yogyakarta, sekolah untuk anak-anak bumiputra. Ia melepas gelar kebangsawanannya dan memakai nama Ki Hajar Dewantara.
caption.en: He came home in 1919, and on 3 July 1922 he founded Taman Siswa in Yogyakarta, a school for Indonesian children. He gave up his noble title and took the name Ki Hajar Dewantara.

caption.id: Pada 1932, aturan baru pemerintah kolonial mengancam sekolah swasta seperti Taman Siswa. Ki Hajar menentangnya tanpa kekerasan, hingga aturan itu akhirnya dicabut.
caption.en: In 1932 a new colonial rule threatened private schools such as Taman Siswa. Ki Hajar opposed it without violence, and the rule was eventually withdrawn.

caption.id: Ia menjadi menteri pendidikan pertama Indonesia, dan hari lahirnya kini diperingati sebagai Hari Pendidikan Nasional. Semboyannya, «Tut Wuri Handayani», berarti mendorong dari belakang.
caption.en: He became Indonesia's first minister of education, and his birthday is now National Education Day. His motto, "Tut Wuri Handayani", means encouraging from behind.

ST-A-HATTA.source: Britannica: Mohammad Hatta; Tirto.id: Cara Hatta membunuh kesepian dalam pembuangan; detik.com: Siapa Bapak Koperasi Indonesia (mengutip Kemendikbud); Antara: Jalan sunyi Hatta hingga Sutami (mengutip Iding Wangsa Widjaja, Mengenang Bung Hatta)

caption.id: Mohammad Hatta lahir di Bukittinggi, Sumatra Barat, pada 12 Agustus 1902. Ia kemudian belajar ilmu ekonomi di Belanda selama sekitar sepuluh tahun.
caption.en: Mohammad Hatta was born in Bukittinggi, West Sumatra, on 12 August 1902. He later studied economics in the Netherlands for about ten years.

caption.id: Karena aktif dalam pergerakan kebangsaan, ia diasingkan ke Boven Digoel di Papua, lalu ke Banda Neira. Ia membawa berpeti-peti buku dan terus membaca serta menulis.
caption.en: Because of his work in the national movement, he was exiled to Boven Digoel in Papua and later to Banda Neira. He took crates of books and kept reading and writing.

caption.id: Pada 17 Agustus 1945, bersama Soekarno, ia memproklamasikan kemerdekaan Indonesia. Ia lalu menjadi wakil presiden pertama Republik Indonesia.
caption.en: On 17 August 1945, together with Sukarno, he proclaimed Indonesia's independence. He then became the Republic's first vice president.

caption.id: Hatta yakin ekonomi rakyat bisa kuat lewat koperasi, yaitu usaha bersama yang saling menolong. Pada Kongres Koperasi 1953 di Bandung, ia dijuluki Bapak Koperasi Indonesia.
caption.en: Hatta believed ordinary people's livelihoods could grow strong through cooperatives, joint businesses built on mutual help. At the 1953 Cooperative Congress in Bandung he was named Father of Indonesian Cooperatives.

caption.id: Hatta dikenal jujur dan sederhana: ia selalu mengembalikan sisa uang negara yang diberikan untuk tugasnya. Ia pernah ingin membeli sepasang sepatu, tetapi uangnya selalu terpakai untuk keperluan lain.
caption.en: Hatta was known for honesty and a simple life: he always returned any unspent state money given for his duties. He once wanted a pair of shoes, but the money always went to other needs.

caption.id: Hatta wafat di Jakarta pada 14 Maret 1980. Teladannya mengajak kita jujur dalam hal kecil, bahkan saat tidak ada yang melihat.
caption.en: Hatta died in Jakarta on 14 March 1980. His example asks us to be honest in small things, even when no one is watching.

ST-A-ZHENG-HE.source: Britannica: Zheng He; Britannica Kids: Zheng He; Visit Jawa Tengah (jatengprov.go.id): Sam Poo Kong

caption.id: Zheng He, yang di Indonesia dikenal sebagai Cheng Ho, lahir sekitar 1371 di Yunnan, Tiongkok, dalam keluarga Muslim. Ia menjadi laksamana kepercayaan kaisar Dinasti Ming.
caption.en: Zheng He, known in Indonesia as Cheng Ho, was born around 1371 in Yunnan, China, into a Muslim family. He became a trusted admiral of the Ming emperor.

caption.id: Pada 1405, kaisar mengutusnya memimpin pelayaran besar ke negeri-negeri di seberang laut. Armada pertamanya terdiri atas 62 kapal besar dan sekitar 27.800 orang.
caption.en: In 1405 the emperor sent him to lead a great voyage to lands across the sea. His first fleet had 62 large ships and about 27,800 people.

caption.id: Antara 1405 dan 1433, armadanya berlayar tujuh kali. Mereka singgah di Jawa, Sumatra, dan Malaka, lalu terus ke India, Teluk Persia, hingga Afrika Timur.
caption.en: Between 1405 and 1433 his fleet made seven voyages. They called at Java, Sumatra and Malacca, then went on to India, the Persian Gulf and as far as East Africa.

caption.id: Pelayaran sejauh itu bergantung pada kompas, pengamatan bintang, dan angin musim. Para pelaut harus sabar menunggu angin yang tepat.
caption.en: Voyages that long depended on the compass, the stars and the monsoon winds. Sailors had to wait patiently for the right wind.

caption.id: Kapal-kapalnya membawa sutra dan porselen, lalu pulang bersama barang dan utusan dari banyak negeri. Zheng He wafat sekitar 1433.
caption.en: His ships carried silk and porcelain and came home with goods and envoys from many lands. Zheng He died around 1433.

caption.id: Di Semarang, kawasan Sam Poo Kong dikaitkan dengan singgahnya Cheng Ho, dan namanya dikenang di banyak kota pesisir. Kisahnya mengajak kita menjalin hubungan dengan bangsa lain secara damai dan saling menghormati.
caption.en: In Semarang, the Sam Poo Kong site is linked to Cheng Ho's visit, and his name is remembered in many coastal towns. His story asks us to build ties with other nations peacefully and with respect.

ST-A-IBN-BATTUTA.source: Britannica: Ibn Battuta; Britannica Kids: Ibn Battuta

caption.id: Ibn Battuta lahir di Tangier, Maroko, pada 24 Februari 1304. Pada 1325, saat berusia 21 tahun, ia berangkat menunaikan ibadah haji ke Makkah.
caption.en: Ibn Battuta was born in Tangier, Morocco, on 24 February 1304. In 1325, aged 21, he set out on the hajj pilgrimage to Mecca.

caption.id: Setelah berhaji, ia tidak langsung pulang. Ia memilih terus berjalan untuk melihat dunia yang lebih luas.
caption.en: After the pilgrimage he did not head home. He chose to keep travelling and see more of the world.

caption.id: Ia menjelajah Afrika Utara, Timur Tengah, dan India. Sekitar 1345 ia singgah di Samudra Pasai, Sumatra, dan sultannya memberinya kapal untuk melanjutkan perjalanan ke Tiongkok.
caption.en: He travelled across North Africa, the Middle East and India. Around 1345 he stopped at Samudra Pasai in Sumatra, where the sultan gave him a ship to continue to China.

caption.id: Perjalanannya panjang dan berat, melintasi gurun dan lautan. Seluruh perjalanannya berlangsung hampir 30 tahun.
caption.en: His journeys were long and hard, across deserts and seas. All together his travels lasted almost 30 years.

caption.id: Atas permintaan sultan Maroko, ia menceritakan perjalanannya kepada penulis Ibn Juzayy. Catatan itu dikenal sebagai Rihla.
caption.en: At the request of Morocco's sultan, he dictated his travels to the writer Ibn Juzayy. The book is known as the Rihla.

caption.id: Ia menempuh sekitar 120.000 km, kira-kira tiga kali keliling Bumi. Kisahnya mengajak kita mengenal dunia dan menghormati orang dari berbagai budaya.
caption.en: He covered about 120,000 km, roughly three times around the Earth. His story asks us to get to know the world and respect people of every culture.

model_answer.id: Benar. Tujuh pelayaran, dari 1405 sampai 1433.
model_answer.en: True. Seven voyages, from 1405 to 1433.

meaning.en: Picture and part of the story.

text.id: Sampai India, Teluk Persia, dan Afrika Timur
text.en: As far as India, the Persian Gulf and East Africa
62 large ships on the first voyage

model_answer.id: Kapal untuk armada besar, kompas untuk arah, dan bola dunia untuk jangkauan pelayarannya.
model_answer.en: Ships for the great fleet, a compass for direction, and a globe for how far he sailed.

meaning.id: Sikap mana yang sejalan dengan kisah ini?
meaning.en: Which attitude fits this story?

text.id: berteman dengan orang dari latar berbeda

model_answer.id: Berteman dengan orang dari latar berbeda: menjalin hubungan dengan saling menghormati.
model_answer.en: Making friends across backgrounds: building ties with respect.

model_answer.id: Ibn Battuta berkelana hampir 30 tahun, singgah di Samudra Pasai, dan kisahnya dicatat dalam Rihla.
model_answer.en: Ibn Battuta travelled for almost 30 years, stopped at Samudra Pasai, and his story was written down as the Rihla.

meaning.en: Earliest first.

text.en: His story written down as the Rihla

model_answer.id: 1304 lahir, 1325 berangkat haji, sekitar 1345 di Samudra Pasai, lalu kisahnya dicatat.
model_answer.en: Born 1304, hajj in 1325, Samudra Pasai around 1345, then his story was written down.

meaning.en: Which picture stands for Ibn Battuta's story?

model_answer.id: Peta rute: ia menempuh sekitar 120.000 km.
model_answer.en: A route map: he covered about 120,000 km.

meaning.id: Ibn Battuta menulis sendiri catatannya setiap hari selama perjalanan.
meaning.en: Ibn Battuta wrote his own notes every day during his travels.

model_answer.id: Salah. Setelah pulang, ia menceritakan perjalanannya kepada Ibn Juzayy, yang menuliskannya menjadi Rihla.
model_answer.en: False. After coming home he dictated his travels to Ibn Juzayy, who wrote them up as the Rihla.

meaning.en: Picture and part of the story.

model_answer.id: Kafilah di gurun, kapal dari Sumatra, dan buku Rihla.
model_answer.en: Caravans in the desert, a ship from Sumatra, and the Rihla.

meaning.en: A good traveller's attitude?

text.en: Looking down on other people's ways
Giving up as soon as you are tired

model_answer.id: Penjelajah yang baik ingin tahu, menghormati tuan rumah, dan sabar.
model_answer.en: A good traveller is curious, respects their hosts and is patient.

meaning.en: Earliest first.

model_answer.id: 1304, sekitar 1345, sekitar 1371, lalu 1405.
model_answer.en: 1304, around 1345, around 1371, then 1405.

meaning.en: Whose story does each picture belong to?

model_answer.id: Zheng He: kapal besar dan kompas. Ibn Battuta: kafilah dan peta rute.
model_answer.en: Zheng He: the great ship and the compass. Ibn Battuta: the caravan and the route map.

meaning.id: Kedua kisah ini mengajak kita menghormati orang dari budaya lain.
meaning.en: Both stories ask us to respect people from other cultures.

model_answer.id: Benar. Keduanya bertemu banyak bangsa dan bertukar barang, kabar, serta ilmu.
model_answer.en: True. Both met many peoples and exchanged goods, news and knowledge.

model_answer.id: Hari Pendidikan Nasional, 2 Mei, adalah hari lahir Ki Hajar Dewantara. Tanggal itu ditetapkan lewat Keputusan Presiden No. 316 Tahun 1959; sebulan sebelumnya, Keppres No. 305 Tahun 1959 mengangkatnya sebagai Pahlawan Nasional.
model_answer.en: National Education Day, 2 May, is Ki Hajar Dewantara's birthday. It was set by Presidential Decree No. 316 of 1959; a month earlier, Decree No. 305 of 1959 had named him a National Hero.

meaning.id: Ki Hajar Dewantara lahir pada 1889 dan mendirikan Taman Siswa pada 1922. Berapa usianya saat itu?
meaning.en: Ki Hajar Dewantara was born in 1889 and founded Taman Siswa in 1922. How old was he then?
